channel.title: NBC Sports Fantasy Football News
channel.description: Latest player news and analysis for fantasy football from NBC Sports.

item.title: Chig Okonkwo (hip) was listed as limited on Monday’s estimated injury report.
item.description: This is a new injury for Okonkwo, who caught a 16-yard pass on the final play of Sunday’s loss to the Rams as the Commanders were looking to tie the game. Okonkwo has gone for 57 or more yards in three of his last four games and would be on the streaming radar as a boom-or-bust TE2 on Thursday against the Giants if he can play.-Zachary Krueger

item.title: Commanders listed Treylon Burks (foot) as DNP on Monday’s estimated injury report.
item.description: Hours after head coach Dan Quinn said he was “optimistic” that Burks would play in Week 10 against the Giants, the Commanders listed him as an estimated DNP for Monday. While they didn’t formally practice, the fact that the team is saying he wouldn’t have gotten on the field today isn’t an encouraging sign for a player who missed all of last week’s practices as well. The good news is there are still more practices to go, meaning Burks could still be upgraded before Thursday night’s game. We’ll see if his status changes on Tuesday when the Commanders take the practice field for the first time on the short week.-Zachary Krueger

item.title: Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said Jake Ferguson (knee) will likely be out “multiple weeks” after going down in Week 9 against the Colts.
item.description: Ferguson exited Sunday’s game against the Colts after taking a nasty hit to his knee. While he was able to walk off under his own power and was later ruled “questionable” to return, the 27-year-old vet never got back into the game. Ferguson has caught just 19 passes for 136 yards and four touchdowns this season, with his best game coming in Week 2 (4-43-2) against the Commanders. Brevyn Spann-Ford, a 2024 UDFA, will likely take over in Ferguson’s absence but shouldn’t be trusted as anything more than a boom-or-bust TE2 at this point.-Zachary Krueger

item.title: Rams head coach Sean McVay said Puka Nacua (knee/turf toe) is likely headed to injured reserve.
item.description: An MRI on Monday revealed a sprained MCL and PCL for Nacua, who also suffered a turf toe injury on the Rams’ final offensive play in Sunday’s win over the Commanders. Nacua caught 14 passes for 150 yards and a touchdown in the win, drawing a target on 44.2 percent of Stafford’s pass attempts. It goes without saying that this creates a massive problem for a Rams’ passing game that has failed to find a serviceable WR2 sans Davante Adams (hamstring). Now, McVay and company will be faced with a new challenge as they try to replace Nacua with the likes of Tutu Atwell, Jordan Whittington, Konata Mumpfield, or a player not yet on the roster. Long believed to be buyers ahead of Tuesday’s trade deadline, it seems like a foregone conclusion that GM Les Snead will do what he can to acquire a playmaker for Matthew Stafford with whatever draft picks he still has at his disposal. The Rams currently only hold own one pick in the first three rounds of the 2027 NFL Draft but still hold their first-round picks in 2028 and 2029, per Spotrac.com.-Zachary Krueger

item.title: Eagles traded DT Jordan Davis to the Jaguars in exchange for a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick.
item.description: While the rest of the league waits to make moves ahead of Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline, the Jaguars have spent Monday wheeling and dealing to improve the defensive side of the ball. Davis is the latest to join the Jaguars, who also acquired S Jessie Bates and DT Davon Godchaux in hopes of shoring up their top-10 defense. Davis signed a three-year, $78 million contract extension with the Eagles earlier this offseason and has been a staple along their defensive line since being drafted 13th overall by them in 2022. Davis has totaled 31 tackles, 1.5 sacks, and two TFLs this season and posted a career-high 4.5 sacks in 2025.-Zachary Krueger

item.title: The NFL reinstated 49ers WR Brandon Aiyuk from the reserve/left squad list.
item.description: According to The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero, the NFL has granted the 49ers a two-week roster exemption for Aiyuk as the two sides continue to negotiate his impending release. The 49ers will have until November 23rd to make a roster move, but once released, Aiyuk will be free to sign with any team. The 28-year-old receiver last played in 2024 and hasn’t taken a snap since tearing his ACL in Week 7 of that season. While there is a chance Aiyuk could suit up for a new team at some point this season, fantasy managers hoping to stash him shouldn’t expect anything meaningful until the fantasy playoffs at the earliest, as it could take him several weeks to find a new team and get up to speed with the season more than halfway over.-Zachary Krueger

item.title: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Gardner Minshew (elbow) could miss Week 10’s game against the Rams.
item.description: Minshew took a hard hit to his right elbow/arm in Sunday’s loss to the Seahawks and is now undergoing tests to determine the severity of his injury. He managed to play through the game, but if he is unable to go in Week 10 against the Rams, rookie Carson Beck would be in line to make his first career start. Minshew threw for 166 scoreless yards against a stout Seahawks defense, but led a comeback victory in just one half of play against the Cowboys the previous week. With recent reports of Michael Wilson (neck) being lost for the season, both Minshew and Beck would be best left on waivers this week.-Zachary Krueger

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Cardinals WR Michael Wilson suffered a neck injury in Week 9’s loss to the Seahawks, ending his season.
item.description: It’s a tough and unexpected loss for the Cardinals, and Wilson, who was not reported to have suffered any injury after the game. Wilson was on track for another solid season after breaking out for 76-1,006-7 last season. He was averaging a solid 9.8 targets per game this season, and never saw fewer than seven targets in any game. Wilson signed a three-year, $75 million contract extension earlier this offseason and will hopefully recover in time to be back for the start of training camp next season. Now without the top three receivers they opened the season with, the Cardinals will likely lean on the trio of Harrison Wallace III, Reggie Virgil, and Simi Fehoko for the remainder of the season.-Zachary Krueger

item.title: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur confirmed Josh Jacobs will undergo surgery on his fractured finger and didn’t rule out a stint on injured reserve.
item.description: LaFleur confirmed previous reports that Jacobs will undergo surgery, but it sounds like he could be at risk of missing more than the three-week “maximum” that was reported. LaFleur not only said a stint on injured reserve was possible, but also noted that Jacobs playing through the injury was never an option, saying he “had no grip strength.” We don’t yet know when Jacobs will undergo his surgery, but LaFleur did confirm that it will be some time this week. With Jacobs now sidelined for the foreseeable future, Green Bay will look to MarShawn Lloyd, Pierre Strong, and Kaleb Johnson to lead the backfield heading into Week 10 against the Vikings.-Zachary Krueger

item.title: Saints head coach Kellen Moore said C Erik McCoy is expected to miss some time with a bicep injury
item.description: McCoy missed 10 games last season due to a torn biceps. It doesn’t sound like his injury is nearly as severe this time around, as Moore said he believes McCoy will avoid surgery. That said, it sounds like the veteran center could be headed for injured reserve with hopes he will return at some point in the season. McCoy has started all eight games he has appeared in this season, earning a PFF grade of 73.2 while allowing just five pressures on 352 pass-blocking downs. He was replaced by Will Sherman in Week 9’s win over the Browns, with Sherman being the favorite to takeover in the weeks ahead while McCoy is sidelined.-Zachary Krueger
